absent: Underlying ring buffer reservation, emission, and completion semantics for forward, backward, and default paths.
Lower layer PMU stop and start behavior for pause and resume indications.
Call history, register snapshot, page extent, address translation, and auxiliary payload helper internals.
Context pinning, iterator traversal order, and system wide versus per task context selection.
Clock source, process identity translation, and trailing identity sample layout.
Address filter stop flag effects and generation counter consumers.
Global interest counter update paths and memory ordering.
Task context data cache lifecycle and attachment failure handling.
Namespace path lookup failure values beyond leaving link info unchanged.
Numeric encodings of record types, misc flags, sample bits, and not available marker.

findings.text: A sample preparation operation enriches a caller supplied sample container using event configuration plus register state. It expands implied dependencies, discards work already marked complete by lower layers, and when nothing remains records the requested type and returns. Otherwise it initializes identity information and conditionally gathers instruction location, call history, raw placeholder, branch placeholder, user register view, interrupt register view, user stack slice, weight, memory origin, transaction state, address values, group identity, page size values, and auxiliary payload, flagging each finished piece and extending dynamic length.

A header preparation operation fills a sample header from prepared data plus owning event plus register state. It marks the record as a sample, computes total length from stable and dynamic portions, derives miscellaneous attributes from event and processor context, and emits a single warning when length is not a multiple of eight.

A shared output routine orders preparation, header creation, space reservation through a caller selected begin method, payload emission, and completion. Three narrow wrappers reuse this order while choosing forward reservation, backward reservation, or default reservation.

Task and system change notifiers broadcast creation and termination, name changes, namespace membership snapshots, and group creation to interested consumers. Each notifier first consults a global interest count and exits promptly when zero, otherwise assembles a temporary carrier on the stack and walks system wide consumers through an iterator with a per event interest test.

Dependency rules enlarge the requested set before collection. Code page measurement implies instruction location, data page measurement or physical location implies virtual address, and user stack implies user registers. Bits already flagged complete are removed from the pending set so earlier driver work is preserved and never repeated.

Dynamic length grows only on first collection of each variable piece. Raw and branch placeholders add one unit each, register views add a descriptor unit plus one unit per requested register actually present, user stack adds a size unit plus payload and length units when the slice is non empty, and auxiliary adds payload plus a size unit. Stack evaluation occurs after other variable pieces because it may consume residual capacity.

Auxiliary length is constrained by residual header capacity under a sixteen bit total, by a per event configured ceiling, and by downward rounding to an eight unit boundary, then finalized by a dedicated auxiliary step that can only retain or shrink. Interrupt register sizing depends on presence of captured state and on a configured mask population count. Physical location derives from virtual address, and page extents derive from address and instruction values.

Output holds a read side critical section from preparation through completion to keep call history storage stable. Execution context replacement, processor wide auxiliary stop, and task data inheritance also employ read side sections around iteration or pointer dereference, paired with matching release operations.

Auxiliary pause entry obtains a ring reference and then enters an interrupt preserving guard. Within the guard it checks a single resume guard flag with ordered loads and stores separated by ordering barriers, exits promptly when already set to prevent recursion from non maskable context, otherwise performs the pause transition and clears the flag before release with reference drop.

Execution time filter maintenance serializes list traversal with an interrupt saving spin lock while resetting file linked ranges and tallying restarts, updates a generation counter under that lock only when resets occurred, and stops the event after unlock. Task data inheritance pairs read side parent lookup with a per processor read guard around child state inspection and conditional attachment.
A read oriented record carries a common header followed by process scope identity and thread scope identity, each thirty two bits wide.

A task transition bundle carries a subject pointer, an optional context pointer, and a creation indicator, plus an embedded fixed record. The embedded record holds a header, subject process and thread identities, ancestor process and thread identities, and a clock value.

A name change bundle carries a subject pointer, a pointer to an aligned name area, the aligned area length, an embedded fixed record with header plus process and thread identities, and an execution origin flag. Total emitted length equals fixed record extent plus aligned name extent.

A namespace snapshot bundle carries a subject pointer plus an embedded record with header, process and thread identities, a slot count, and one link element per namespace slot. Each link element receives device and inode numbers from a namespace path lookup on success and remains unchanged on lookup failure.

A group creation bundle carries a path pointer and path length plus an embedded record with header, numeric group identity, and flexible trailing path storage. A remote stop bundle pairs a ring pointer with an error accumulator. An iterator callback accepts an event pointer and opaque caller data and produces no result.

Auxiliary capture toggles between running and paused per hardware state. Pause acts only from running, setting paused and requesting underlying stop with pause semantics. Resume acts only from paused, clearing paused and requesting underlying start with resume semantics. Duplicate requests leave state unchanged.

On execution replacement, every file linked filter slot is cleared to empty origin and zero extent with a restart tally incremented per slot, and a generation value advances once when the tally is non zero. Advancement triggers a stop of the owning event after lock release.

Public sample emission entries each take an event, sample data, and register state. Default emission returns a status code, while forward and backward variants choose directional reservation without returning status.

Public lifecycle entries cover task creation notification, current task execution replacement, task name change with execution origin indication, namespace snapshot for a task, and parent to child task data propagation during creation. All tolerate absence of interested consumers or missing context by returning without side effects.

Header extent handling assumes eight unit alignment and sixteen bit capacity. Misalignment and auxiliary inclusive overflow each trigger a one time warning without local correction, leaving any policy response to callers or operators.

Group path handling allocates a full path buffer and substitutes a short placeholder literal when allocation fails. Emitted path extent is padded upward to eight unit alignment with explicit zero fill to prevent leakage of stale tail bytes, and the buffer is freed after broadcast.

Auxiliary pause tolerates absent input by warning once on null event and by silent return on missing ring reference. Inherited auxiliary stop resolves absent parent linkage to the event itself and tests parent ring association under read side protection, relying on output reassignment to stop before repointing to close a documented race.

Record type facts observed: samples use a sample marker, task creation and termination use distinct fork and exit markers, name changes use a comm marker with a separate misc flag for execution origin, namespace snapshots use a namespaces marker, and group creation uses a group marker. Interest in each stream is gated by a dedicated per event attribute bit.

Sample flag facts observed: instruction location, call history, raw payload, branch history, user registers, interrupt registers, user stack, weight, memory origin, transaction, address, physical address, group identity, data page extent, code page extent, and auxiliary payload each have a request bit plus a completion bit. Observed initial values are zero for weight and transaction and address, a not available marker for memory origin, empty placeholders with reserved length for raw and branch, and current group identity for group samples.
